incubation_period.value: 1 to 3 days, with illness typically lasting 2 to 3 weeks

diagnosis.value: Isolating the bacteria from affected birds, supported by clinical signs and PCR testing

treatment_overview.value: Early antibiotic treatment given promptly can help affected birds recover, though the disease can return once medication stops

when_to_call_vet.value: Call a vet if birds develop facial swelling with nasal discharge and sneezing, since prompt treatment improves recovery and a lab test is needed to tell it apart from similar respiratory diseases.

summary.value: Infectious coryza is a contagious bacterial respiratory disease of chickens that causes facial swelling, nasal discharge and sneezing, and can sharply cut egg production in laying hens. It is not a risk to human health, and control relies on biosecurity, vaccination in high-risk areas, and prompt antibiotic treatment.
